1.explanation:
1. src/language-js/needs-parens.js contains the core logic for whether to preserve or drop parentheses around expressions. Currently it doesn’t treat a JSDoc `@satisfies` comment as a reason to keep the wrapping `(…)`, so it unconditionally removes the parens on an object literal.
2. src/language-js/utils/is-type-cast-comment.js only recognizes `@type` in block comments as a cast that should retain parentheses. It needs to be extended (or a parallel helper added) to detect `@satisfies` so the printer knows this comment means “don’t drop parens.”
3. src/language-js/printer-estree.js (in functions like `genericPrint` and `printPathNoParens`) orchestrates how comments and parentheses are applied to AST nodes. Because it assumes type‐cast comments are only `@type`, it ends up calling the “no‐parens” branch when it sees `@satisfies`, causing the dropped parentheses. Adjusting these branches to honor the extended comment detection will fix the formatting issue.
